findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical signed-counter design. A move updates exactly its row, column, and applicable diagonals, and an absolute total of n is an exact win certificate under valid unique moves. The state and adapter are concise and conventional, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 348 and its Python TicTacToe surface. The Reference preserves valid alternating moves, unique cells, no post-win calls, all winning lines, the adapter contract, the fully illustrated source example, and all five constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064532047. Its signed change, row and column updates, diagonal guards, absolute-total win check, and return values align exactly with the protected app-local class; the solve dispatcher is the only substantive adapter.

The former largest tier used illegal n=128 beyond the source maximum of 100. The replacement 6, 24, and 96 tiers remain legal, span 16x, and make one valid non-winning move in every row and column. The current source passes all nine executions at +0.00 relative growth and 1.01x; correct full-line counting passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.87 and 18.04x.

The Approach accurately derives signed line totals, proves cancellation cannot conceal a win, and states O(1) per move, O(m) total time, and O(n) space. Its edge discussion now respects the legal n>=2 contract instead of claiming a 1 x 1 board.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the complete source example and board sequence, all five constraints, move and winner semantics, and the source-native follow-up.

coverage: The sole authenticated Premium operation-sequence example appears first with its exact board size, chronological moves, and per-move statuses.
The invented minimum-board row win is now a trial, and the illegal n=1 row was removed because the source requires n>=2.
The former n=2 player-two column case was invalid because player one had already won on move three; it was replaced by a legal n=3 sequence whose first winner is player two on move six.
Visible trials cover the minimum board n=2, maximum board n=100, coordinates zero and n-1, and a legal nine-move n=3 draw that reaches the n-squared call bound.

Player-one and player-two wins across rows, columns, the main diagonal, and the anti-diagonal are covered, including an odd-board center that belongs to both diagonals and mixed counters that must not report a false win.

An independent stored-board line scan verified all nine authored results and all three benchmarks; the target also matched it on 73,489 exhaustive legal alternating game prefixes and a legal 199-move n=100 row win.
All nine correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged legal n=6, n=24, and n=96 non-winning workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
